title: Deploy-halt decision ladder and incident communication templates
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a lightweight decision ladder (stop/go/halt/escalate) for runtime-1.24 deploys, formalize release-blocker criteria, and ship ready-to-use incident communication templates for on-call, PMs, and GTM. Aim to reduce ambiguity during canary and early ramp and shorten time-to-decision for rollback or mitigation.
objectives: Define clear, measurable release-blocker criteria tied to telemetry
Produce a single-page decision ladder (who decides, windows, thresholds, next actions)
Author 3 severity-based communication templates (P0/P1/P2) for internal and external stakeholders
Integrate templates into the release checklist and the Console release notes flow
acceptance_criteria: Decision ladder accepted by Eng leads (runtime & infra) and SRE
Templates reviewed and approved by Comms and Legal for customer-facing copy
Release-blocker list added to the runtime-1.24 gating checklist and enforced by launch coordinator
Playbook snippets pushed to the release runbook and linked from the CI release pipeline
release_blockers: Canary error rate > 1.5x baseline for 10+ minutes after smoothing
Median p50 tail latency increase > 2x on serving-critical paths for 5 minutes
KV cache corruption observed in > 0.1% of requests (detected by regression tests)
Unauthorized access events (audit logs show failed RBAC enforcement)
Data exfiltration or clear PII leakage reported from canary traces
gating_metrics: Errors: 5xx rate (canary / baseline) over 10m and 1h windows
Latency: p95 and p99 token generation time per model family
Cost: abnormal spikes in GPU utilization (>90% sustained) impacting other tenants
Quality: sample prompt evaluation regressions >1.5x failure rate compared to baseline prompts
rollback_plan: Primary: immediate automated rollback to previous pinned model image with traffic cut to 0% for runtime-1.24, open incident channel, notify stakeholders. Secondary: if automated rollback fails, escalate to SRE lead to execute hotfix or partial region drain. Triage must capture root cause and determine if forward-fix is acceptable; rollback remains default for customer-impacting regressions.
comm_templates:
P0 INTERNAL: Subject: [P0][runtime-1.24] Immediate deploy halt and rollback
Audience: Execs, Eng leads, SRE, PMs, Support lead
Body: We have halted the runtime-1.24 deploy due to a P0 signal ({{metric}} exceeded threshold). Automated rollback initiated to previous image as of {{timestamp}}. On-call: {{oncall_name}}. Next steps: SRE is collecting logs and a postmortem will be started within 2 hours. Customer-facing comms are being drafted. Triage channel: #inc-runtime-1-24-p0

P1 INTERNAL -> EXTERNAL: Subject: [INCIDENT][runtime-1.24] Service degradation detected (canary)
Audience: Eng leads, Support, Customer Success, Affected customers list
Body: We detected elevated error rates in canary traffic starting {{timestamp}}. We have paused the roll for canary and are investigating. No widespread customer impact observed yet. Support runbook: use internal template to respond to inbound tickets. We'll send an update within 60 minutes or earlier if conditions change.

P2 EXTERNAL: Subject: [Notice] Temporary increase in latency for some model responses
Audience: Subscribed customers, status.redwood.ai
Body: We are monitoring a temporary increase in response latency for a small subset of requests following a deployment test. Our team is investigating and applying mitigations; customers should see normal service shortly. Subscribe to status for updates.
stakeholder_matrix: Launch Coordinator: Slack @launch-coordinator channel / 0-5m updates during critical window
SRE Lead: Pager duty / escalate immediately for P0/P1 incidents
Engineering Lead (runtime): Responsible for go/no-go decision after canary window
PM Lead: Customer comms owner for external notifications
GTM/Comms: Prepare external language and approval path within 30 minutes of rollout halt
Support: Triage incoming tickets using canned responses; escalate to PM for sensitive customers
